key_insight: The simplified Phan-Thien-Tanner (sPTT) model predicts a purely elastic centre-mode instability in both channel and pipe flows, highlighting the importance of transient rheology.
engineering_relevance: These predictions could help anticipate viscoelastic flow instabilities under realistic operating conditions and distinguish constitutive models with identical steady rheology.
method: Numerically analyse linear stability of pressure-driven channel and pipe flows.
Use the sPTT constitutive model in the absence of inertia.
Contrast instability predictions with Oldroyd-B and FENE-P models.
evidence_signal: Numerical results identify instability across a wide range of polymer concentrations and at much lower Weissenberg numbers than previously predicted for purely elastic channel-flow instability.
watch_item: Experimental validation is needed; linear instability alone does not establish the subsequent nonlinear or chaotic flow behaviour.
paper_title: Purely elastic centre-mode instability in channel and pipe flows of a simplified Phan-Thien-Tanner fluid
